meta.description: Hand-authored Altium Develop enrichment overlays (strategic subset). Transcripts are pedagogical outlines unless marked verbatim.

overlays.shortDescription: Orient to Altium Develop as a multidisciplinary hardware workspace—not just another CAD install.
overlays.fullSummary: This introduction positions Altium Develop for hardware teams that need shared visibility across electrical, mechanical, procurement, and leadership. You will leave with a mental model of workspaces, projects, collaboration surfaces, and how Develop complements Altium Designer rather than replacing schematic/PCB craft.
learningOutcomes: Explain what Altium Develop is for and who it serves on a hardware team
Distinguish Develop collaboration surfaces from desktop CAD editing
Identify the first workspace/project actions to take after watching
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with electronics product development roles

chapters.title: Why Develop exists for modern hardware teams
Who collaborates: ECAD, MCAD, sourcing, leadership
What to do next: first workspace setup

transcript.text: [Outline] Altium Develop is framed as a connected hardware workspace for multidisciplinary teams—not a replacement for deep PCB layout skill.
[Outline] Workspaces hold people and permissions; projects hold design artifacts, history, and review threads.
[Outline] Non-CAD stakeholders need browser-visible status without installing Designer.
[Outline] Recommended next step: download/setup walkthrough, then create your first team workspace.

overlays.shortDescription: Follow work from a Jira ticket to a released PCB—closing the loop between program tracking and Develop.
overlays.fullSummary: End-to-end delivery narrative: ticket intake, design execution in the hub, reviews, BOM risk, and release—so program tools and engineering truth stay aligned. Highlights integration points and manual discipline where automation ends.
learningOutcomes: Map a Jira (or equivalent) ticket to Develop project activity
Keep ticket status honest using hub evidence
Close tickets only against released or explicitly accepted revisions

transcript.text: [Outline] Tickets without hub evidence become fiction.
[Outline] Link ticket IDs in commit/release notes.
[Outline] Do not mark done at 'layout finished'—wait for release gates.
[Outline] Productivity practices next help sustain the system.

proceduralSteps.detail: Put ticket ID in project notes / release notes.

proceduralSteps.title: Update ticket from hub
proceduralSteps.detail: Status changes cite history/review links.

proceduralSteps.title: Close on release
proceduralSteps.detail: Only after Develop release (or accepted defer).

overlays.shortDescription: Best practices for hardware team productivity—focus, WIP limits, and Develop as the operating system.
overlays.fullSummary: Productivity without burnout theater: fewer parallel boards, clearer owners, faster reviews, and Develop hygiene that reduces context switching. Prepares managers to coach teams at scale.
learningOutcomes: Apply WIP limits to boards and open review threads
Identify productivity leaks (meetings, rework, unclear owners)
Install a weekly Develop operating rhythm

transcript.text: [Outline] More parallel PCBs often means less throughput.
[Outline] Cap open review threads per designer.
[Outline] Measure review latency using unresolved comments age.
[Outline] Coaching/scaling lesson generalizes these practices.

proceduralSteps.title: Set WIP caps
proceduralSteps.detail: Boards in flight + open threads.

proceduralSteps.title: Publish review SLA
proceduralSteps.detail: e.g., 48h for critical comments.

proceduralSteps.title: Weekly rhythm
proceduralSteps.detail: History + comments + release candidates.

overlays.shortDescription: Coach teams and scale Develop best practices so good habits survive growth and new hires.
overlays.fullSummary: Leadership capstone for this Develop enrichment set: turning local pilot habits into team standards—onboarding checklists, review norms, release discipline—and using Develop itself as the training ground via past projects and visible exemplars.
learningOutcomes: Codify Develop operating standards for your org
Coach new hires using live project history and exemplars
Scale practices without drowning teams in process docs

transcript.text: [Outline] Scaling fails when standards live only in a manager’s head.
[Outline] Coach on real threads/history—not abstract slides.
[Outline] New-hire checklist: workspace, comments, release rules.
[Outline] Loop back to intro lessons when rebooting a team’s mental model.
